name: Samhain
date_note: October 31 to November 1. Some traditions observe it on November 1.
history: Irish Samhain foods were built around the late harvest. Colcannon and barmbrack are the best-documented dishes. Folk accounts describe small charms or trinkets hidden in them as fortune-telling. Some sources also note meatless fare on the vigil of All Saints, which is one reason cabbage and potato dishes became common.
confidence: Well documented for Ireland. Modern customs are blended with Halloween.

sources.title: The Journal: Halloween foods and the vigil of All Saints

dishes.name: Colcannon
dishes.ritual_note: Folk accounts describe small charms hidden in the mash. Skip charms for children and guests who might choke. A simpler custom is to serve a well of butter in the centre.
ingredients: 1.5 kg floury potatoes, peeled and quartered
300 g savoy cabbage or kale, shredded
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for about 20 minutes, until soft. Drain well.
Cook the cabbage or kale in a little salted water for 4 to 5 minutes, then drain.
Warm the milk with the spring onions and 30 g of the butter over low heat for 2 minutes.
Mash the potatoes with the warm milk mixture. Fold in the greens and season to taste.
Spoon into a bowl and make a well in the centre. Melt the remaining butter and pour it in.
dishes.safety: Let guests know before serving if you hide anything in the dish.

dishes.name: Barmbrack (speckled fruit loaf)
dishes.ritual_note: Traditional barmbrack hid charms inside. Use slips of paper wrapped in baking parchment and tell the guests first.
steps: Soak the dried fruit in the cold tea overnight, then drain any extra liquid.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and spice. Add the warm milk, egg and melted butter, then knead for 8 minutes into a smooth dough.
Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour, until doubled.
Knead the drained fruit into the dough, then shape it into a round and place it in a greased 20 cm tin.
Cover and prove for 45 minutes. Bake at 180 C for 50 to 60 minutes, until it sounds hollow when tapped.
Brush with the warm honey while hot and cool on a rack.
dishes.safety: Serve sliced and spread with butter, with strong tea, as is traditional.
